prints.catalogue_details: Engraving, ca. 1560’s. Bartsch 52; Bellini 5, second state; Lewis, Lewis and Boorsch A2, second state, with the inscription lower left. In the shaded area lower right the initials “M.D.” are clearly visible, which they are not generally, in the second state. In L, L & B they are interpreted as Ghisi’s monogram in reverse, though they acknowledge this is outside the norm in his work. R.E. Lewis accepted the work as by Ghisi (as did Bartsch), while Boorsch found the style slightly freer than his work of this date.

prints.page: SIRANI Giovanni Judith with head of Holofernes.html
prints.catalogue_details: Etching. The Illustrated Bartsch 1 (314); Gori Gandellini XIV, 192, as a firm attribution; Marcus Sopher (Seventeenth Century Italian Prints, 1978) 75, as very plausible; Bertelà/Ferrari 929, as possibly Sirani Sopher mentions an early impression or state before horizontal scratches in the drapery. While our impression has a few plate scratches, it does not appear to have the ones referred to. Sopher also illustrates an undescribed anonymous reverse copy of much the same size.

prints.catalogue_details: Etching, 1637. Bartsch XX, 70, 17. The print was designed in two plates, divided neatly by the balustrade, this being the lower half. This impression was clearly never separated from a second sheet, but with most of the figures occupying this part of the composition, it becomes a stand-alone image.
